analysis: Both units are base_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 428-612 and 612 onward), documentation only, with no code, configuration, or mode/rename metadata changes visible. They describe release-candidate and shipped changes (v0.9.10 live model switching, App Attest key rotation/recovery, diagnostics, v0.9.9, v0.9.8, v0.9.7 MDM-optional authorization, the account-scoped first-content SLA, and earlier items). The entries are consistent with the canonical model on TB-002/TB-009/TB-011 and T-052..T-058: diagnostics are untrusted and non-authorizing, rotation never revokes or denies serving, rotated keys must pass full attestation, receipt, build-qualification and assertion checks, and revocation fences final handoff. No threat-model assumption is contradicted by the text. I could not review the underlying source changes, so the behavior described in these changelog entries remains unvalidated against code. A later source pass should check three items: the App Attest key rotation admission and budget logic, the live model switch routing fence, and the public model-demand suppression thresholds (minimum 20 requests and 3 accounts). The changelog alone offers no concrete security regression.
